newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche says FDA recommends Posicor approval.
newsitem.headline: Roche says FDA recommends Posicor approval.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said a U.S. Food and Drug Administration medical advisory panel had recommended approving its Posicor drug (Mibefradil) for the treatment of high blood pressure and chronic stable angina.
"The panel recommendation represents a milestone for Roche," it said in a statement.

"After the FDA gives final approval for Posicor, Roche's presence in the heart-circulatory sector will be significantly strengthened, even more so given Roche's pushing ahead with additional cardiovascluar medicines."
Posicor, a new calcium channel antagonist, has already been approved for use in the Netherlands and Switzerland, it said.
Clinical studies show the drug is at least as good if not better than other calcium antagonists, it said. More clinical tests are under way, with final results expected in mid-1998.
Credit Suisse First Boston said in a recent equity analysis of Roche shares that clinical trial results for Posicor had shown favourable results for hypertension and angina.
"We have estimated peak sales at 700 million Swiss francs, but Roche's own estimate of 800 million plus is not unreasonable," it said.

Pictet & Cie said Posicor faced a tough marketing battle if Roche was to hit its 800 million sales target within five years. "We are expecting a launch in H2 1997 and are forecasting sales of 450 million francs by 2001 based on a gradual but steady pick-up," it said.
